nodes.title: Pydantic AI Graph (beta) - Persistence and Resumability

nodes.text: LangGraph's BaseCheckpointSaver protocol is put (checkpoint + metadata + new channel versions), put_writes (intermediate per-task writes), get_tuple (returns CheckpointTuple or None, pending_writes in writes_sort_key order) and list (filter, before, limit), each with an async twin (aput, aput_writes, aget_tuple, alist), plus get_next_version (monotonic, default int +1). Base methods raise NotImplementedError until a saver implements them.

LangGraph durability has three modes: exit (persist only when the graph exits, so a mid-run crash is unrecoverable), async (persist while the next step runs, so the latest checkpoint can be lost on a crash) and sync (persist before the next step starts, highest durability, some cost).
On resume from a super-step, LangGraph keeps pending writes of nodes that completed in that super-step, so completed nodes are not re-run. Resume granularity is the node/super-step, not mid-node.

The reference savers: InMemorySaver stores checkpoints in RAM; SqliteSaver is for lightweight synchronous use, is thread-locked, has no async support, and keeps checkpoints and writes tables keyed (thread_id, checkpoint_ns, checkpoint_id[, task_id, idx]) with serialized blobs; PostgresSaver is documented as the production option. The docs state no formal per-saver durability guarantees.
nodes.limitations: PostgresSaver source (transactions, put_writes atomicity) not read; only the docs' positioning.

nodes.text: LangGraph's default JsonPlusSerializer is msgpack-based with typed ext codes (constructors, Pydantic v1/v2, numpy, delta snapshot); pickle is off by default (pickle_fallback=False) and enabled explicitly. Unregistered types are allowed with a warning in permissive mode and blocked (raw data returned) when an allowlist or strict mode applies; an allowlist (allowed_msgpack_modules) exists. Optional encryption is available through EncryptedSerializer passed as serde.
nodes.limitations: Strict-mode default flips in future versions (warning says 'blocked in a future version'); version-specific.

nodes.text: LangGraph schema evolution: renaming or removing a node can fail resume for threads paused at that node; adding optional state fields and rewiring edges between surviving nodes are safe (edge topology is not persisted); removing/renaming/tightening a state field breaks older checkpoints. Recommended: deprecate before delete, rename in stages, stamp a version flag at thread start.
nodes.limitations: A single practitioner post claims the rename failure is silent (resume does nothing) rather than an error; not verified here.

nodes.text: Pydantic-AI removed pydantic_graph.persistence (BaseStatePersistence and file/in-memory implementations) in V2; graph state is no longer snapshotted, because of the complexity of consistent snapshotting under parallel execution. This contradicts the hypothesis that pydantic_graph still ships a persistence protocol.
nodes.limitations: Docs say removed in V2; the v1 BaseStatePersistence/NodeSnapshot API was not fetched, so its shape is unverified here.

nodes.text: Pydantic-AI replaced graph persistence with a Harness capability StepPersistence: an async StepStore Protocol (about ten methods) with InMemory, File, Sqlite, Mongo and Postgres backends. Snapshots of message history are written after each tool-call step whose calls have all returned and on failure; continue_run returns the latest complete snapshot's messages, fork_run branches, a missing snapshot raises LookupError, and an in-flight step is not retried automatically (tool effects stay 'started' in a ledger). Snapshots exclude mid-step state, capability state and workspace files.
nodes.limitations: Docs page summarized by the fetch tool; package is 0.x and the API may change between minor releases. Persists message history, not arbitrary workflow state.

nodes.text: StepPersistence stores JSON (files: run.json, events.jsonl, snapshots/{seq}.json; SQLite with messages keyed by SHA-256) with a content-addressed media marker whose format is versioned; compatibility is upgrade-only and an unknown marker version raises ValueError. Old SQLite DBs get new columns on open (additive migration on open).

Pydantic-AI delegates whole-run crash survival to durable execution engines (Temporal, DBOS, Prefect, Restate and others): the engine journals model requests and wrapped tool calls, replays completed steps after restart and retries the in-flight one; non-durable tools run in workflow code on each replay and must be deterministic.

OpenAI Agents SDK has no checkpoint store protocol in the pages read: RunState is a serializable snapshot (to_json/to_string, from_json/from_string, result.to_state(), resume via Runner.run(agent, state)) used for paused runs (approvals) and cancel(mode="after_turn"); the application owns storage. Docs warn to deserialize only trusted snapshots. Durable engines (Temporal, DBOS, Dapr, Restate) are external integrations.
nodes.limitations: Absence of a store was inferred from two docs pages; RunState schema versioning not checked. The HITL page itself does not mention Temporal/DBOS; the running-agents page does.

nodes.text: Common pattern across the three libraries: checkpoint at a completed-step boundary and keep the store interface small and async (LangGraph: put/put_writes/get_tuple/list; Pydantic-AI: about ten-method StepStore; OpenAI: app-owned RunState blob), and delegate whole-run durability to external durable engines. Pydantic-AI deliberately dropped arbitrary graph-state checkpointing because of parallel execution.

For a single-instance host, a core checkpoint protocol should be minimal: save(run_id, step snapshot), latest(run_id), list/history and writes keyed by (run_id, step_id), JSON-only serialization with an explicit schema-version field and no pickle by default, and a reference SQLite/file backend; defer pending-writes (parallel branches) and durability modes unless parallel nodes are supported.
What is the exact v1 pydantic_graph BaseStatePersistence/NodeSnapshot/EndSnapshot API and semantics (superseded by removal in V2)? Does PostgresSaver commit writes and checkpoints atomically?
